title: Adaptive throttle dashboard scenarios and sketches
body:
Purpose:
Short exploratory doc to capture UX ideas and backlog candidates for a dashboard that helps customers understand and manage adaptive throttles (per-key, per-route) and quota fallbacks. Focus is on observability + explainability (why a request was throttled, what policy acted, and how to mitigate).

High-level goals:
- Make throttles transparent: show why and when a key or route hit soft vs hard limits.
- Surface cost/latency tradeoffs that drive adaptive throttles.
- Provide interactive tools to test policy changes (simulator) before rollout.
- Reduce noise: group related events, highlight top causal paths.

Personas:
- Platform engineer (SRE) debugging spikes across multiple customers. Wants root causes, quick drilldowns, and a sandbox to validate fixes.
- Product engineer (integrator) owning a single API key/route. Wants per-key guidance, temporary rate increases, and clear action items to avoid customer-facing errors.
- Ops/Security reviewer. Wants audit trails and tamper-proof logs for quota changes.

Scenarios to support (concrete examples):
1) Sudden token spike on route /v1/chat (customer A): dashboard shows per-route time-series, top contributing API keys, and request fingerprints (short prompt signature). Show correlated CPU/gpu queue length and latency. Recommend rollout: increase soft-burst by +20% for 10m and re-evaluate.
2) Noisy key with inconsistent patterns: key X toggles between normal and abusive behavior. UI surfaces pattern (repeating short bursts every 15s), suggests policy: enable burst-smoothing + enable per-key adaptive-scaling with stricter decay.
3) Graceful degradation: capacity constrained region triggers fallback policy (model downgrade). Show side-by-side: predicted latency/cost impact if we downgrade to quantized-variant. Allow one-click apply to a single credential for 30m.

Wireframe / interaction notes (visuals are rough, written for engineers):
- Top-of-page summary card: current throttle state (green/yellow/red), top-3 impacted routes, number of keys affected, a single-sentence rationale (e.g., "adaptive-throttle triggered by 3x baseline token rate and GPU queue >80% for 2m").
- Time-series panel: stacked area chart for total tokens/s, broken down by route. Hover shows per-key breakdown and sample request IDs. Include time-range quick buttons (1m, 15m, 1h, 24h).
- Per-route detail pane: latency histogram, error rate, throttle-events heatmap (minute granularity), and a table: [api_key, avg_tokens_per_req, requests/min, throttle_count, last_throttle_time, policy_version]. Table rows expandable to show last 10 example prompts (redacted).
- Per-key mini-profile: quota allotment, burst credits remaining, applied policies, last policy-eval trace. Button: "simulate + apply" which opens a modal (see simulator).
- Simulator modal: slider for traffic increase, checkboxes for policies (burst credits, adaptive scaling, hard limit), preview of expected throttle events and cost delta. Optionally run a short synthetic test in sandbox to collect traces.
- Explainability timeline: a waterfall view showing which rule fired in order (rate-limit -> fallback -> model-downgrade), with timestamps and short rationale text.

Data model & instrumentation needs (what backend should provide):
- Per-request meta: timestamp, route, api_key_hash, token_count, latency_ms, node_id, model_variant, policy_id, evaluation_result (allow/soft-block/hard-block), sampling_id.
- Policy traces: evaluation steps, matched condition, threshold values, and decision TTL.
- Aggregates: per-minute and per-second counters for tokens, requests, throttle events by (route, key, region, model_variant).
- Cost attribution: per-token cost model by model_variant and GPU-hour baseline for reconciliation.

Edge cases and privacy/PII: 
- Never store full prompts in the UI. Show deterministic redacted snippets or hashed fingerprints. Allow customer opt-in for full diagnostic payloads with explicit consent and retention limits.
- When key owners rotate credentials, map historical data to previous keys only if mapping metadata is available.

Backlog (priority + rough estimate):
- RT-1: Time-series + stacked breakdown by route/key (MVP) — 2 sprints.
- RT-2: Per-key policy trace + explainability timeline — 1.5 sprints.
- RT-3: Interactive simulator with quick apply to single key (safe defaults + audit log) — 2 sprints.
- RT-4: Sampled example requests panel (redaction pipeline + storage) — 1 sprint (compliance review needed).
- RT-5: Cost impact preview (model downgrade cost delta) and one-click fallback toggle — 1 sprint.
- RT-6: Alerting templates for "key approaching soft limit" with recommended remediation — 0.5 sprint.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Default sampling rate for request examples (1/100? configurable per org?).
- Do we expose burst-credit counts directly or an abstract "available headroom"? Transparency vs gameability tradeoff.
- Approval flow for one-click applies — role-based and must generate audit event.

Acceptance criteria for MVP (RT-1 + RT-2):
- Dashboard shows live tokens/s with per-route breakdown and per-key table; hover to see last 5 sampled request fingerprints.
- For any throttle event, user can click to view a policy trace that explains which condition matched.
- Simulator can estimate throttle count when increasing traffic by X% for 10m (based on historical-shaped traffic).

Notes from grooming meeting (2025-11-07):
- Taylor: prioritize policies audit trail; legal wants 1y retention for policy decisions.
- Marco: prefer server-side sampling of request bodies, only surface small redacted snippets; storage costs are a concern.
- Priya: instrument telemetry to capture queued-request-length metric from serving runtime; that is a leading indicator for adaptive throttle.

Quick UX experiments (A/B ideas):
A) Show raw burst-credit number vs a normalized "headroom score" (0-100). Measure whether ops actually use the number to tune policies.
B) Default to grouped alerts (by route) with an option to "expand to keys" — see if this reduces alert fatigue.

Deliverables for next sync:
- Low-fidelity mockups for summary card and per-route pane (Taylor).
- Backend contract doc: aggregated metrics and policy trace schema (Marco).
- Compliance checklist for sampled request storage (Priya).

Reference links and related tickets: CONFLUENCE-5642 (policy-trace-spec), JIRA-RT-1127 (throttle-sim feature request), github.com/redwood-inference/rate-sim/pull/34 (prototype sim).

End notes: aim for a lightweight, testable surface first — the biggest wins are reducing time-to-detect (SLO->throttle link) and minimizing noisy alerts. Keep simulator tied to historical shape to avoid false confidence.
